title: Panigang Best Chili (Panigang Best F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Panigang Best chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Panigang Best chili is an F1 hybrid chili variety, also sold or known as Panigang Best F1 or Condor Panigang Best. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor brand).

heroImage.alt: A farmer watering vegetable beds in Pulilan, Bulacan, the kind of farm where Panigang Best chili is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Panigang Best F1 or Condor Panigang Best, this is the same chili. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [chili variety finder](/crop-varieties/chili), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: first harvest 50 to 55 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chili fields most often: [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [Corn earworm](/pests/corn-earworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 50 to 55 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Siling haba (pansigang) type: glossy light green, 13 to 15 cm long, about 13 g, red when ripe, only slightly hot.
**Where:** Lowland, also grown on hill farms in Laguna.
Keeps for up to about a week after picking, so it ships well.
Also bore well on a hilly farm in Laguna, where the plants grew taller than in the lowland.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: Agriculture Monthly profiled a Liliw, Laguna hill farm picking 300 to 400 kg a month from half a hectare, and a Batangas chili grower planted it around his field, also in Harbest's Seeds of Hope catalogue. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual chili on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Panigang Best chili

Decide first between siling haba, the long green finger chili for cooking, and siling labuyo, the small hot one. Hybrids bear more and for longer, while open pollinated labuyo keeps its heat and lets you save seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.

items.q: Is Panigang Best F1 the same as Panigang Best?
items.a: Yes. Panigang Best F1 is another name for Panigang Best. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Panigang Best?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
